_comment: How the daemon builds a sub-identity registration that names a referrer. Captured from verusd 1.2.17-2 on VRSCTEST, 2026-07-29, with registeridentity's `returntx` flag so nothing was broadcast.
_finding: A referral on a sub-identity is RECORDED IN THE RESERVATION AND PAID NOTHING. The referred and unreferred registrations under the same parent are structurally identical: the full fee to the parent as a reserve output, no payout output, and exactly idimportfees consumed natively. There is no discount either. This is unlike a chain-level registration, where a referral both discounts the fee and pays the referrers.

parent.name: sdkcuralpha
parent._note: 3 referral levels, so the currency does pay referrers for something — just not for this.

referrer.name: sdkrefa.sdkcuralpha.VRSCTEST@
referrer._note: Registered on VRSCTEST purely to have a referrer to name.

outputs._note: the daemon packs native and reserve change into one output; this SDK emits two, which consensus also accepts — see the on-chain sub-identity 4e746e10d67c9815e46b9bdb0ac3ec7fd41d432fa76b1f9895ce66ec7b560b45

conservation._note: exactly idimportfees; the reserve is fully conserved, 99.0 in and 99.0 out

unreferred_control.name: sdkrefc
unreferred_control._why: the same registration with no referrer, to prove the referral changes nothing

_proofprotocol_probe._comment: The refusal of parents whose proofprotocol is not 2 was justified by 'a fractional parent needs a CReserveTransfer'. That reasoning does not hold; the refusal remains only because no reference transaction exists.

VRSCTEST._note: an ordinary chain-level registration is already a registration under a proofprotocol 1 parent

Royal1._note: a token, NOT fractional, and it accepts a name commitment as a parent

kmerg._note: refuses outright: 'kmerg is unable to issue currencies', so the gate is the options, not the proof protocol

_proofprotocol_probe._blocked_on: a sub-identity registration under a proofprotocol 1 token parent needs that parent's tokens to pay the fee; none are held on any node available here
